name: Speyer Cathedral
description: Rising above the town of Speyer in Germany's Rhine valley, this vast red sandstone cathedral was begun in 1030 by Emperor Conrad II. Its four towers and two domes crown a soaring Romanesque basilica with a vaulted nave, finished in the early 12th century. For almost 300 years it served as the burial place of German emperors, and with Cluny's abbey in ruins it is the largest surviving Romanesque church.
